mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 101 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS), indicates supply-side stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 101 AND RSAFS < previous month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of falling energy prices.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 0.5% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month by > 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) due to labor force re-entry indicates a positive labor market dynamic masked by broader participation, which supports consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE > previous month for one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.8% for three consecutive months signals improving supply capacity, which lowers input costs and boosts profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month by > 0.8% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
